thread:
Alex Chen: heads up — we got a page from oncall-bot about sustained queue backlog on inference-prod around 12:08 PDT. spike in queued_requests and a few customer throttle events. looks like autoscaling didn't react quickly enough. paging now for oncall handoff.

oncall-bot: ALERT: inference-prod queued_requests > 400 for 7m (hosts: gpu-pool-03) :rotating_light:
  summary: 'High queue depth on inference-prod'
  link: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/1769998887

Priya Kapoor: I'm on it, digging into metrics. quick question — how many customers affected? any 5xxs?

Michael Torres: seeing elevated throttles in the proxy logs — snippet:
```
2026-03-11T19:06:12Z proxy[abcd] WARN throttle_event customer_id=acct_92 tokens=1200 reason=burst_limit
2026-03-11T19:07:03Z proxy[abcd] WARN throttle_event customer_id=acct_18 tokens=3400 reason=capacity_shed
```
no hard 500s surfaced, latencies increased to ~750ms p95 for a subset of routes.

Samir Patel: gpu-pool-03 nodes show spike in kernel latency and GPU queue depth. autoscaler logs show scale decision at 12:12 but new nodes still provisioning. looks like cold-start time ~4m under current instance type.

Priya Kapoor: Customer impact: two mid-market customers reported degraded responses (long tails). I reached out to SEs and flagged for potential SLA touchpoint.

Alex Chen: immediate mitigation — reduce batch sizes and enable synchronous fallback for high-latency routes to lower queue growth. can we push a hotfix config?

Michael Torres: deploying rolling change to routing config to switch these routes to lower-batch-profile now. command: `curl -X POST https://deploy.local/config -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","batch_profile":"low-latency"}'`

Priya Kapoor: also increasing autoscaler aggressiveness for gpu-pool-03 as temporary measure: change threshold queued_requests > 200 over 2m -> trigger additional scale. propose we use this for 1 hour and then roll back.

Alex Chen: agree. but we need to tune alerts — paging on queued_requests > 400 for 7m produced a lot of noise previously. this incident shows we under-alerted for earlier rise. want to propose layered alerts and clearer paging policy.

Samir Patel: suggested alert set:
- P0 page: queued_requests > 250 for 5m AND throttle_count > 5 in 5m -> page oncall
- P1 ops channel: queued_requests > 150 for 10m OR tokens_per_sec drop > 30% for 10m -> notify eng-sre but not page
- P2 metric: GPU kernel latency p95 > 200ms for 10m -> create dashboard row and Slack message (no page)

Michael Torres: here's a draft Datadog monitor rule we can use (copy/paste):
```yaml
name: "Inference -> High queue with throttles"
query: "avg(last_5m):sum:inference.queued_requests{env:prod,pool:gpu-pool-03} by {pool} > 250 && sum(last_5m):sum:inference.throttle_events{env:prod,pool:gpu-pool-03} by {pool} > 5"
options:
  notify_audit: false
  timeout_h: 1
  notify_no_data: false
  escalation_message: "Paging SRE: possible capacity saturation. See runbook: https://ops.redwood.example/runbooks/capacity-saturation"
```

Priya Kapoor: love that. Also propose a synthetic guard: tokens_per_sec across region < 50% of baseline for > 5m -> create Ops notification so product can triage customer-facing degradation.

Alex Chen: we should also add a short-lived dashboard for this incident with three rows: queued_requests heatmap, throttle_events top-k customers, tokens_per_sec over time. Samir — can you create and share snapshot?

Samir Patel: creating dashboard now and will share link in thread. also adding a log re-run query to identify top 10 customer_ids by throttle events: `logs.query("service:proxy AND throttle_event", limit: 1000) | top(customer_id, count)`

oncall-bot: NOTE: scale action executed at 12:12, +4 nodes requested. estimated ready: 12:16.

Michael Torres: routing change deployed at 12:14, batch size for /v1/generate moved from 64 -> 16 for flagged routes. early signs: queued_requests dropping from 420 -> 180 over next 3 minutes.

Priya Kapoor: Customers acked improved behavior from SEs. sending post-incident customer note draft to #customer-success.

Alex Chen: post-incident action items (assign owners):
- Tune alerts as Samir suggested and update paging rules (owner: Priya)
- Add dashboard row + retention view (owner: Samir)
- Investigate autoscaler cold-start for this instance type and evaluate faster instance types or warm pool (owner: Michael)
- Create runbook section for rapid batch-size override and routing fallback (owner: Alex)
- Post-mortem writeup and impact timeline (owner: Priya)

Samir Patel: noted. I'll update alert configs in staging and open a PR with the Datadog YAML. PR link: https://git.redwood.example/alerts/PR-4219

Michael Torres: logging note — we should add a throttle reason tag to make post-incident triage faster (reason: capacity_shed | burst_limit | policy). filing quick ticket.

Priya Kapoor: immediate follow-up: setting temporary monitor thresholds now and tagging them `incident-temporary`. will revert after postmortem.

Alex Chen: thanks everyone. capture timeline in incident channel and assign 2-hour follow-up review tomorrow 10:00am PT. if anyone sees regression roll back the batch override and scale down extra nodes after traffic normalizes. :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: dashboard: https://ops.redwood.example/dashboards/dash-8142 (shared) — includes heatmap and top-k throttled customers. saved snapshot and pinned to the thread.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: resolved — queued_requests normalized at 12:20. incident duration 12:08-12:20. follow-ups required.

Alex Chen: filing the post-incident checklist now and assigning owners in the ticket tracker. Thanks all for quick response.

Priya Kapoor: adding postmortem tags and linking the alert PR. I'll draft customer-facing note after we have the impact table.

Michael Torres: I'll take the autoscaler investigation as part of my next sprint.

Samir Patel: closing ops tasks on my side, will keep the PR open for review.

Alex Chen: natural language summary for the writeup: brief cause = capacity saturation + slow node provisioning; mitigation = routing -> low-batch, temporary aggressive scaling, cleared; long-term = alert tuning, warm pool or faster instance, dashboard & runbook updates.

Priya Kapoor: good summary. I'll turn that into the postmortem body.

Alex Chen: thread archived for now — we'll reconvene in the postmortem meeting.
